title: Exploratory Analysis of a Multimodal Sensor Prototype During Pediatric Tooth Extraction: A Preregistered Pilot Study with Protocol Deviations
content: Objective physiological monitoring may complement self-report during pediatric dental procedures, but a multimodal prototype requires careful characterization before any diagnostic evaluation. This exploratory, post hoc analysis of summary case-report-form data from a preregistered pilot study (Open Science Framework, DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/S8H4D) describes phase-related physiological responses during tooth extraction and baseline agreement between the prototype and comparator instruments. The primary cohort comprised 43 children aged 8–12 years; a sensitivity cohort added seven 7-year-old protocol deviations (n = 50). The preregistered feasibility, safety, progression, and Modified Venham outcomes were unavailable and are not reported. Galvanic skin response (GSR), heart rate, skin temperature, and blood pressure increased during extraction and partly returned toward baseline during recovery (Friedman χ2 = 55.39–86.00; all p < 0.001). The GSR rank order was identical in every participant, and heart-rate values were identical across devices; neither pattern could be explained from the available records. Baseline intraclass correlation coefficients for GSR, skin temperature, and blood pressure were 0.994–0.998 but rest on unverified summary values. These findings are hypothesis-generating and cannot establish feasibility, safety, or diagnostic validity; verification against raw device records is required.
